$$f(n) = 512^{n_1} f(n_1) = 512^{n_1+n_2} f(n_2) = \cdots = 512^{n_1+n_2+\cdots+n_m}$$
where $n_m$ is the first value $< 10$ (the leading digit), at which point $f(n_m) = 512^0 f(0) = 1$.

Since $n_i = \lfloor n/10^i \rfloor$, we get
$$f(n) = 512^{S(n)}, \quad S(n) := \sum_{i\ge 1}\left\lfloor \frac{n}{10^i}\right\rfloor.$$
(For $n=0$, $S(0)=0$ and $f(0)=1=512^0$, consistent.)

Writing $n = \sum_{j\ge 0} d_j 10^j$ in decimal, one checks:
$$S(n) = \sum_{j\ge 1} d_j \cdot \frac{10^j-1}{9} = d_1\cdot 1 + d_2\cdot 11 + d_3\cdot 111 + d_4\cdot 1111 + \cdots$$

## Step 2: Hexadecimal digit count

Since $512 = 2^9$, we have $f(n) = 2^{9S(n)}$. The number of base-16 digits of $2^k$ is $\lfloor k/4\rfloor + 1$ (since $\log_{16}2 = 1/4$). So
$$\text{(hex digits of }f(n)\text{)} = \left\lfloor \frac{9S(n)}{4}\right\rfloor + 1.$$

We need this $\le 2500$:
$$\left\lfloor \frac{9S}{4}\right\rfloor \le 2499 \iff \frac{9S}{4} < 2500 \iff S < \frac{10000}{9} \approx 1111.11 \iff S \le 1111.$$

$$d_1 + 11d_2 + 111d_3 + 1111d_4 \le 1111.$$

**Case $d_4 = 1$:** Need $d_1 + 11d_2 + 111d_3 \le 0$, forcing $d_1=d_2=d_3=0$. **1 solution**.
